story.head: Unstoppable force vs. immovable object
paras: The Flames (10-12-1) lost 4-1 to Minnesota on Thursday, and the Senators (14-6-3) lost 6-5 in overtime to Philadelphia the same night. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Senators third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).
The Flames’ record (.457) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.674) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.603), largely because they’re 7-3 in one-goal games.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so good looks are likely to be hard to come by for them. Calgary has scored 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Senators forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and get into a lot of chippy games (3rd). Something has to give when the Flames’ shooting runs into the Sens’ defense.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 23 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (11 G / 17 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Dustin Wolf (5-6-1 / .877 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for Calgary. Linus Ullmark (10-1-0 / .940 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Ottawa and will likely start.
The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.

The Senators have been without Warren Foegele, Jonas Johansson and William Eklund for several games. Linus Ullmark is expected to start.
Yegor Sharangovich has four goals in six games against Ottawa since 2023-24.
Fabian Zetterlund has two goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
